# Medusa — Student Setup Guide

This is a **course fork of [medusajs/medusa](https://github.com/medusajs/medusa)** — the open-source
commerce **framework monorepo** (30+ TypeScript packages). It is pinned to a verified baseline:

- **Version:** `@medusajs/medusa` **2.17.2**
- **Baseline commit:** `8f97e3f371`
- Everyone starts from this exact commit. Do **not** pull from upstream `develop`/`main` — it moves and can break.

📚 **Official documentation:** <https://docs.medusajs.com>

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Tool | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Node.js** | **20 LTS or 22 LTS** | Do not use Node 24 — a few test suites fail on it. Use [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm). |
| **Corepack** | ships with Node | Run `corepack enable` — it activates the repo-pinned **Yarn 3.2.1** automatically. Do not install Yarn globally. |
| **Docker** | any recent | Only needed for **integration tests** (and for running a real store DB). |
| **Git** | any | |

> 💡 **New to Turborepo or Yarn workspaces?** This monorepo holds 30+ TypeScript packages built with [Turborepo](https://turbo.build/repo/docs). The key things to know: always run commands from the repo root; use `yarn workspace @medusajs/<name> <command>` to target one package; and run `yarn build` after install — packages depend on each other's build output.

> 📖 **Architecture overview:** [docs.medusajs.com/learn](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn) explains the module system, commerce modules, and how the packages fit together. Read the *Framework* section before exploring the source.

**OS:** Linux, macOS, or **Windows via WSL2** recommended.

---

## 2. First-time setup

```bash
git clone <your-team-fork-url>
cd medusa
corepack enable          # activates Yarn 3.2.1 from the repo
yarn install             # ~1-2 min
yarn build               # ~4 min — builds all 80 packages; REQUIRED before running tests
```

`yarn install` prints ~19 warnings (native-module "must be built" notices + one TS compat-patch
line) — these are **benign**. `yarn build` should end with `80 successful, 80 total`.

---

## 3. Start the project

```bash
# Admin dashboard dev server (Vite):
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev

# Design-system component explorer (Storybook, http://localhost:6006):
yarn workspace @medusajs/ui storybook

# Full store + admin with seed data (needs the Postgres from step 5):
npx create-medusa-app@latest my-store \
  --db-url "[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]://[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@localhost:5433/my_store"
cd my-store && yarn dev        # admin at http://localhost:9000/app
```

---

## 4. Testing — backend (Jest) & frontend (Vitest)

```bash
# FULL unit baseline across all packages. KEEP --continue:
# plain `yarn test` aborts on the first failing package and won't run the rest.
yarn turbo run test --no-daemon --no-cache --force --continue

# A single package:
yarn workspace @medusajs/order test        # backend (Jest)
yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard test    # frontend (Vitest)
yarn workspace @medusajs/ui test           # frontend (Vitest)

# A single file:
yarn jest <path/to/file.spec.ts>
```

---

## 5. Testing — integration (needs Docker)

Start a Postgres (and Redis, only for the `*-redis` modules) on non-default host ports:

```bash
docker run -d --name medusa-pg -e POSTGRES_USER=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] -p 5433:5432 [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:16-alpine
docker run -d --name medusa-redis -p 6380:6379 redis:7-alpine
```

Run integration tests with the DB env vars (the runner creates throwaway temp DBs):

```bash
# Git Bash / Linux / macOS:
DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] DB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] \
  yarn workspace @medusajs/region test:integration     # one module (verified: 18/18)

# Whole suites (long; `modules` also uses Redis):
DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] DB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] yarn test:integration:modules
DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433 DB_USERNAME=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] DB_PASSWORD=[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri] yarn test:integration:http
```

$env:DB_HOST="localhost"; $env:DB_PORT="5433"; $env:DB_USERNAME="[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]"; $env:DB_PASSWORD="[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]"
yarn workspace @medusajs/region test:integration
```

Teardown: `docker rm -f medusa-pg medusa-redis`

## Contributing workflow

All team members have write access to this repository, so the team uses a **branch-based** workflow — not forks. Here is the background and the commands.

**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you _don't_ have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.

**Branch-based workflow** is what most professional teams use internally. You clone the shared repo once, create a short-lived branch for each issue, push the branch back to the same repo, and open a PR from that branch into `main`. One clone, one remote, full PR workflow.

### For each issue you work on

```bash
# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)
git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa.git
cd medusa

# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main
git checkout main
git pull origin main

# Create a branch named for the issue
git checkout -b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      # new feature
git checkout -b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   # bug fix

# ... make your changes, run tests ...

# Stage and commit
git add <the files you changed>
git commit -m "feat: add dark mode toggle (#17)"

# Push the branch to the team repo
git push origin feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

After pushing, GitHub shows a **"Compare & pull request"** banner on the repository page. Click it to open a PR from your branch into `main`. Fill in the description (what changed and why), reference the issue (`Closes #17`), and request a review from a teammate.

**Branch naming:**

| Prefix | Use for |
|---|---|
| `feat/issue-<N>-short-description` | new features |
| `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` | bug fixes |
| `chore/short-description` | docs, config, dependency updates |

> ⚠️ **`main` is protected — direct pushes are blocked.** All changes go through a reviewed PR. If you accidentally commit to `main` locally, move your changes to a branch before pushing:
>
> ```bash
> git checkout -b fix/issue-42-my-fix   # create branch from your current state
> git checkout main
> git reset --hard origin/main          # revert local main to match remote
> ```

**After your PR is merged**, delete the branch to keep the repo tidy:

```bash
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-17-dark-mode
```

## 6. Project documentation & policies (required reading)

📚 **Official documentation:** <https://docs.medusajs.com> — framework concepts at
[docs.medusajs.com/learn](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn), API reference at
[docs.medusajs.com/api](https://docs.medusajs.com/api).

Medusa has its own established contribution processes. They are **not restated here** — you are
responsible for finding, reading, and following them from the sources below:

| You must take care of | Where to find it |
| --- | --- |
| How to use the tool | <https://docs.medusajs.com> |
| Code review process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Pull Requests](CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests) |
| Bug / issue resolution process | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Issues before PRs](CONTRIBUTING.md#issues-before-prs) |
| Pull request conventions & PR policies | [CONTRIBUTING.md — Workflow](CONTRIBUTING.md#workflow) (branches, commits, PRs) |
| AI policies | [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md) (this repo's AI conventions); check [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the current policy |

**Coding Conventions:**

- Formatting (Prettier): no semicolons, double quotes, 2 space indentation, ES5 trailing commas, always use parentheses in arrow functions  
- Naming convention:   
  - Files: kebab-case (define-config.ts)  
  - Types/Interfaces/Classes: PascalCase  
  - Functions/Variables: camelCase  
  - Constants: SCREAMING\_SNAKE\_CASE  
  - DB fields: snake\_case

**Branching and Commit Conventions:**

- All changes should be part of a branch and submitted as a pull request \- your branches should be prefixed with one of: fix/ for bug fixes, feat/ for features, or docs/ for documentation changes.  
    
  \# One-time setup: clone the team repo (skip if already done)  
  git clone https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/medusa.git  
  cd medusa  
    
  \# Before starting each issue: make sure you are on a fresh main  
  git checkout main  
  git pull origin main  
    
  \# Create a branch named for the issue  
  git checkout \-b feat/issue-17-dark-mode      \# new feature  
  git checkout \-b fix/issue-42-toast-dismiss   \# bug fix  
    
  \# ... make your changes, run tests ...  
    
  \# Stage and commit  
  git add \<the files you changed\>  
  git commit \-m "feat: add dark mode toggle (\#17)"  
    
  \# Push the branch to the team repo

## What it already covers
| STUDENTS.md requirement | Container |
|---|---|
| Node 20 or 22 LTS (not 24) | `typescript-node:22` image, currently v22.23.2 |
| `corepack enable` and Yarn 3.2.1 | Done in `postCreateCommand`; `yarn -v` shows 3.2.1 |
| `yarn install && yarn build` | Done in `postCreateCommand` |
| Postgres 16 for integration tests | `[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:16-alpine` service, with `DB_HOST`/`DB_PORT`/`DB_USERNAME`/`DB_PASSWORD` set in `remoteEnv` |
| Redis 7 for the `*-redis` modules | `redis:7-alpine` service |
| Dashboard (5173), Storybook (6006), store admin (9000) | All three ports are forwarded |
| Git and `gh` for the branch/PR workflow | Both installed |
| Prettier and ESLint conventions ([standards.md](docs/sprint0/standards.md)) | Both extensions installed |

## Gaps in the container
1. **`REDIS_URL` isn't set.** The Redis integration tests fall back to `redis://localhost:6379` ([workflow-engine-redis database.ts:14](packages/modules/workflow-engine-redis/integration-tests/utils/database.ts#L14), [locking-redis spec:18](packages/modules/providers/locking-redis/integration-tests/__tests__/index.spec.ts#L18)). Inside the container Redis lives at `redis:6379`, so those tests will fail in `test:integration:modules`. Fix: add `"REDIS_URL": "redis://redis:6379"` to `remoteEnv`.
2. **Port 8000 isn't forwarded.** That's the Next.js storefront in `my-store`, and the store's CORS settings expect it.
3. **`my-store` isn't shared.** It's excluded in `.git/info/exclude`, so it only exists on your machine. Each teammate has to run `create-medusa-app` themselves, and nothing in the container does that for them.
4. **Minor:** `server.open: true` in the dashboard Vite config tries to open a browser inside the container. It's harmless but prints noise. Also, `SpecStory.specstory-vscode` doesn't appear in any setup doc. That's fine if it's meant for saving chats to `ai-logs/`, but it's worth mentioning to the team.

## Where STUDENTS.md is wrong inside the container
- **Section 5** says to `docker run` Postgres and Redis on host ports 5433/6380, and to prefix test commands with `DB_HOST=localhost DB_PORT=5433`. Inside the container both are wrong: those prefixes override the correct `remoteEnv` values and the tests won't reach the database. In the container you just run `yarn workspace @medusajs/region test:integration` with no prefix.
- **Section 3** uses `--db-url [REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]://...@localhost:5433/...`. Inside the container this should be `[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]://[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]@[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]:5432/my_store`, which is what your local `my-store/apps/backend/.env` already uses.
- **Port mismatch:** the container publishes Postgres on host port **5434** (commit e1be8f0cd0), but STUDENTS.md uses **5433** for the non-container path. Both work, but it's confusing. Either pick one or say which applies where.
- STUDENTS.md doesn't mention the dev container at all, so students won't know it exists or how to use it.

## Not related to the container
Your working tree also has the [vite.config.mts](packages/admin/dashboard/vite.config.mts) `esbuild.define` change plus two leftover `vite.config.*.tmp.mts` files. You'll probably want to keep those out of this `chore/dev-container` branch.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-03 17:41:14Z)**_

Each port belongs to one of the dev servers in STUDENTS.md, plus the storefront in `my-store`:

| Port | What runs there | How it starts |
|---|---|---|
| **9000** | Medusa backend, with the store admin at `/app` | `cd my-store && yarn dev` (STUDENTS.md section 3) |
| **8000** | Next.js storefront in `my-store` | Started by the same `yarn dev`; its script is `next dev -p 8000` |
| **5173** | Admin dashboard Vite dev server | `yarn workspace @medusajs/dashboard dev` (section 3; 5173 is Vite's default) |
| **6006** | Storybook for the design system | `yarn workspace @medusajs/ui storybook` (section 3; its script uses `-p 6006`) |

These servers run inside the container. Listing the ports in `forwardPorts` makes VS Code map each one to the same number on your laptop, so URLs like `http://localhost:9000/app` and `http://localhost:6006` from STUDENTS.md work in your normal browser. VS Code often forwards ports automatically when it sees a server start. Listing them explicitly keeps the port numbers the same for everyone and means they're forwarded from the moment the container opens.

The original file had 9000, 5173 and 6006. I added 8000 because the storefront runs there, and the backend's `STORE_CORS` setting already expects `http://localhost:8000`.

Postgres and Redis aren't in this list on purpose. Inside the container they're already on `localhost:5433` and `localhost:6379`. _**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-03 17:42:04Z)**_

Docker is still being used. You just don't start those containers yourself anymore.

The dev container is itself built from Docker. When VS Code opens the project, it reads [docker-compose.yml](.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml) and starts three containers together:

| Container | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `app` | Your laptop's Node/Yarn setup. VS Code, the terminal and `yarn` all run in here. |
| `[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]` | `medusa-pg`, which you started with `docker run` in STUDENTS.md section 5 |
| `redis` | `medusa-redis`, also from section 5 |

So the two containers you used to run by hand are still there. Docker Compose now starts them automatically every time you open the dev container, and stops them when you close it. Because the three share one network, `app` reaches Postgres at `localhost:5433` and Redis at `localhost:6379`. Those match the addresses from your old manual setup, which is why the commands in STUDENTS.md still work unchanged.

To see them, run `docker ps` in a terminal on your laptop, not inside the container. You'll see three containers with names like `medusa_devcontainer-app-1`, `-[REDACTED:generic-credential-uri]-1` and `-redis-1`.

You don't need the old `medusa-pg` and `medusa-redis` containers when you work in the dev container. You can leave them as they are: the dev container publishes on 5434 and 6381, so the ports don't clash. Or you can remove them with `docker rm -f medusa-pg medusa-redis`. Keep them only if you sometimes work outside the dev container.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-03 17:59:12Z)**_

This PR doesn't need a changeset. A changeset records a version bump for a published `@medusajs/*` package, and that note ends up in the release changelog. Your PR only touches `.devcontainer/` files, which aren't part of any package, so there's nothing to bump. Leave that checklist box unticked with the "not needed" note I already put in the summary.

If a reviewer or a CI check insists on one anyway, add an empty changeset. It satisfies the check without bumping any package:

```bash
yarn changeset --empty
```

That creates a file with a random name in `.changeset/`. Commit it with the rest of the PR.

For future PRs that do change package code, such as a feature in `packages/admin/dashboard`:

```bash
yarn changeset
```

1. Use space to select the packages you changed, then press enter.
2. Skip the **major** and **minor** prompts by pressing enter on each, so the change counts as a **patch**, as the PR template asks.
3. Type a one-line summary, for example `feat(dashboard): add low stock indicator`.
4. Commit the new `.changeset/*.md` file with your changes.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-10-05 23:08:44Z)**_

I made the fix in [docker-compose.yml:30-31](.devcontainer/docker-compose.yml#L30-L31):

```yaml
